title: Prostate biopsy
what: With a thin needle, the doctor takes a few small pieces of prostate tissue to check under a microscope. The needle is guided by ultrasound.
why: Most often for a raised PSA blood test, or changes found on an exam or a prostate MRI.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 15 to 30 minutes
tell_doctor: Blood thinners and aspirin. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Allergies, especially to antibiotics or numbing medicines
If you have a fever or a urine infection right now
If you have artificial heart valves or joint replacements

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: A urine test and blood tests are usually done before the biopsy, and sometimes an MRI. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Antibiotic
prepare.text: An antibiotic is often prescribed to protect against infection. Take it exactly as the doctor says.

prepare.title: Bowel
prepare.text: If the biopsy is done through the rectum, you often need an enema or suppositories. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: A light breakfast is usually fine. If you will have sedation or anesthesia, do not eat for a few hours before. Your clinic will tell you the time.

bring: Your PSA results and prostate MRI
Someone to go with you, if you will have sedation
steps: You lie on your side with your knees to your chest, or on your back with your legs raised
You get pain relief: a numbing injection, or general anesthesia
A thin ultrasound probe is put into the rectum
The doctor takes a few tissue samples with a needle, through the bowel wall or through the skin between the legs
Each sample is a short click of the device
The probe is removed and the area is cleaned
feel: The probe in the rectum feels like pressure and discomfort
Each sample is a click and a quick sting. It is usually bearable
Afterwards, a dull ache low down may last a day or two
after: Blood in your urine and stool can appear for a few days
Blood in your semen can last a few weeks. This is usually not dangerous
Drink more water for the first few days
No heavy lifting or sport for a few days
The result usually comes in 1 to 2 weeks. The doctor will explain it
red_flags: A temperature above 38 degrees or chills: see a doctor right away or call emergency services. This may be an infection
A lot of blood or clots in your urine, or bleeding from the rectum that does not stop

faq.a: Pain relief is usually given. You feel pressure and clicks. Most men cope with it calmly.

faq.q: Is blood in semen after a biopsy normal?
faq.a: Yes, it can last a few weeks. If there are clots in your urine, tell your doctor.

reminders.text: Prostate biopsy tomorrow. Start the antibiotic and bowel prep, if your doctor prescribed them. Bring your test results and MRI.
